labelPolicy.positive: DONKI links the flare, directly or through one linked CME, to at least one SEP record observed by an instrument
labelPolicy.ambiguous: the linked SEP records are all model output or of unknown origin; excluded from training and testing, never counted as negative
labelPolicy.negative: no qualifying recorded SEP association; this is not proof that no particle event occurred

instrumentInventory.instrument: Space Environment In-Situ Suite on the GOES-R series satellites; its proton sensor is the SGPS
instrumentInventory.basis: NOAA documents SEISS as a particle instrument whose SGPS measures protons in place from 1 to 500 MeV, and NOAA publishes integral proton fluxes at and above 10 MeV as observed on the primary GOES satellite.
instrumentInventory.recordContext: The name gives a satellite, an instrument and an integral proton channel, and carries no MODEL: prefix. DONKI does not say what the P in GOES-P stands for; reading it as the primary GOES satellite is our reading, not a documented fact.

instrumentInventory.instrument: COSTEP on SOHO; its EPHIN sensor measures electrons, protons and helium
instrumentInventory.basis: The instrument team documents COSTEP as measuring energetic particles from the Sun, with EPHIN covering hydrogen from 4 to more than 53 MeV, which contains this channel. The page does not list this channel itself.
